propositions.text: The claimant is 26 years old, Mexican citizen, claiming refugee protection based on membership in the social group of homosexuals under IRPA sections 96 and 97.
propositions.quote: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, the claimant, 26 years old, a citizen of Mexico, is basing his refugee protection claim on sections 96-membership in the particular social group of homosexuals-and 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

propositions.text: The claimant alleges facts in support of his refugee protection claim.
propositions.quote: In support of his claim, he is alleging the following facts.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant, a 26-year-old Mexican, claims refugee protection as a homosexual under IRPA sections 96 and 97, alleging supporting facts.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges he is homosexual and his problems with his lover began in 2008.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleged that he is homosexual and that his problems with his lover began in XXXX 2008.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he is homosexual and his problems with his lover began in 2008.

propositions.text: The claimant had a romantic relationship with XXXX since 2006.
propositions.quote: He had been in a romantic relationship with XXXX since XXX 2006.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges a romantic relationship with XXXX since 2006.

propositions.text: In March 2008, the claimant met a prominent politician XXXX who showed interest and they started a secret affair a month later.
propositions.quote: In March 2008, he met a prominent politician, XXXX, at the XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX. XXXXX displayed an interest in the claimant by giving him expensive presents and asking him out several times. A month later, they became lovers and started having a secret affair because of XXXXX high social standing in the community.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges meeting politician XXXX in 2008, starting a secret affair due to XXXX's high social standing.

propositions.text: The claimant ended the relationship because he was ashamed of deceiving XXXX; XXXX then harassed him and threatened to get rid of him.
propositions.quote: The claimant ended this relationship with XXXXX because he was not proud of deceiving XXXXX. XXXX was offended and started harassing the claimant. One day, he told the claimant that he was going to get rid of XXXX because he could not let go of his relationship with the claimant.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant ended the relationship; XXXX was offended, harassed, and threatened him.

propositions.text: The claimant began noticing strange people near where he and XXXX lived.
propositions.quote: At this time, the claimant began noticing strange people where he and XXXX lived.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant noticed strange people near his residence with XXXX.

propositions.text: The claimant warned XXXX he would reveal evidence of their relationship if XXXX did not stop harassing him.
propositions.quote: Tired of the threats, the claimant warned XXXXX that if he did not leave him alone, he would reveal the cards, gifts and photographs that XXXXX had given him-undeniable evidence of the relationship that would damage XXXXX image in the community.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant warned XXXX he would expose evidence of their relationship if harassment continued.

propositions.text: Police informed the claimant that XXXX was killed; claimant identified the body but did not report threats due to police mockery.
propositions.quote: A few days later, the police called the claimant to tell him that XXXX had been killed. The claimant went to the police station to identify the body. The claimant wanted to report XXXXX threats to the police, but he changed his mind when they made fun of him after he told them that XXXX was his lover.

paragraphs.summary: Police told claimant XXXX was killed; claimant identified body but did not report threats due to police mockery.

propositions.text: The claimant went to live with a friend; XXXX called to warn he knew claimant's location and threatened him to return or be killed.
propositions.quote: The claimant went to live with a friend. The next day, XXXXX called the claimant on his cellphone to warn him that he knew where he was. The claimant went to seek refuge in the city of XXXXX. However, two days later, XXXXX called him again. He said that it was his last chance to go back to him; if he refused, he would kill him that same day.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant sought refuge after XXXX threatened to kill him if he did not return.

propositions.text: Claimant changed phone number and traveled to XXXXXXXX; XXXX called again threatening to kill within 24 hours.
propositions.quote: The claimant immediately his changed telephone number and travelled to XXXXXXXX. However, six days later, XXXXX called him on his cellphone again and warned him that he was going to kill him within 24 hours.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant changed phone number and location; XXXX threatened to kill him within 24 hours.

propositions.text: Fearing for his life, the claimant left Mexico in 2008.
propositions.quote: Fearing for his life, the claimant left his country on XXXXX, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant fled Mexico in 2008 fearing for his life.

propositions.text: The claimant claimed refugee protection in Montréal on June 27, 2008.
propositions.quote: He claimed refugee protection in Montréal on June 27, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant filed refugee protection claim in Montréal on June 27, 2008.

propositions.text: The panel determines the claim cannot be allowed after hearing testimony and analyzing evidence.
propositions.quote: After hearing the claimant's testimony and analyzing all of the evidence, the panel determines that this claim cannot be allowed, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The panel decides the refugee claim is not allowed after hearing testimony and evidence.

propositions.text: The claimant's marriage in Montréal in 2010 establishes nexus with membership in the social group of homosexuals under section 96.
propositions.quote: Based on the claimant's testimony, according to which he married XXXXX on XXXXXX, 2010, in Montréal, the panel concludes that there is a nexus with one of the five grounds in section 96, that is, membership in the particular social group of homosexuals.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's marriage in Montréal establishes nexus with the social group of homosexuals under section 96.

propositions.text: The claimant's identity was established to the panel's satisfaction with Mexican passport seized by CIC and copies on file.
propositions.quote: The claimant's identity was established to the panel's satisfaction. He appeared before the authorities at the port of entry with his Mexican passport, which was seized by Citizenship and Immigration Canada (CIC), and copies of which are on file.

paragraphs.summary: The panel is satisfied the claimant's identity is established by his Mexican passport and CIC records.

propositions.text: The claimant's testimony was not credible, with examples to follow.
propositions.quote: The claimant's testimony was not credible. The following are some examples.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's testimony not credible, providing examples.

propositions.text: The claimant fears XXXX will kill him if he returns to Mexico.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that he still fears XXXXX because he is convinced that this individual will kill him as soon as he returns to Mexico.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant fears XXXX will kill him upon return to Mexico.

propositions.text: The claimant testified XXXX is a well-known politician in XXXXX and belongs to the 'XXX' party, which he described as XXXXXXXXXXX XXXXX with XXXX in 2008.
propositions.quote: When asked about XXXXX profile, the claimant testified that he is a well-known politician in XXXXX. When asked what political party XXXXX belongs to, the claimant answered the "XXX"; when asked what this acronym stood for, the claimant stated that it stood for the XXXXXXXXXXX XXXXX and that XXXXX had XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX 2008.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified XXXX is a well-known politician belonging to 'XXX' party, described as XXXXXXXXXXX XXXXX with XXXX in 2008.

propositions.text: The panel could not find a party called 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' in the evidence; the party XXX is the second-largest parliamentary group in Mexico's chamber of deputies.
propositions.quote: Despite the extensive amount of evidence submitted as A-1, the panel could not find a party called the [translation] "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX." The documentary evidence indicates that the Party XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, abbreviated XXX, is the second-largest parliamentary group in Mexico's chamber of deputies.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no party called 'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX'; XXX is the second-largest parliamentary group in Mexico's chamber of deputies.

propositions.text: No evidence corroborates claimant's statements about XXXX's political role; XXXX is not currently part of Mexico's political scene.
propositions.quote: In addition, there is no information on a politician named XXXXXXXXXX in the extensive evidence entered on the record. Furthermore, there is no evidence to corroborate the claimant's statements that XXXXX was XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX in 2008. Consequently, the panel is of the opinion, based on the fact that XXXXX is not mentioned in the documentary evidence submitted and on a balance of probabilities, that XXXXX is not currently part of the political scene in Mexico.

propositions.text: This lack of corroboration leads the panel to question the truthfulness of the claimant's entire story.
propositions.quote: This leads the panel to question the truthfulness of the claimant's entire story. The following analysis supports this conclusion.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no evidence supports claimant's statements about XXXX's political role and questions the claimant's story truthfulness.

propositions.text: Claimant testified affair with XXXXX began and ended by telephone in 2008.
propositions.quote: the claimant testified that his affair with this individual began on XXXXX, 2008, and that he ended the relationship by telephone on XXXXX, 2008.

propositions.text: Claimant said XXXXX sometimes accompanied him to his door.
propositions.quote: he answered that XXXXX sometimes accompanied him to his door.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified his affair with XXXXX began and ended in 2008 and that XXXXX sometimes accompanied him to his door.

propositions.text: Claimant testified next face-to-face meeting with XXXXX was in 2008 at his workplace.
propositions.quote: the claimant testified that his next face-to-face meeting with XXXXX was on XXXXX, 2008, at the XXXXXXXXXXXXXX, where the claimant worked.

propositions.text: On that date, XXXXX mentioned he was going to get rid of XXXXX.
propositions.quote: He also testified that it was on this date that XXXXX had mentioned that he was going to get rid of XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified his next meeting with XXXXX was in 2008 at work, where XXXXX said he would get rid of XXXXX.

propositions.text: Claimant noticed strange people in a pickup truck outside his home in 2008, identified as XXXXX employees and security staff.
propositions.quote: he had noticed strange people in a pickup truck outside his home. He added that these were XXXXX employees... these people were members of XXXXX security staff.

propositions.text: Six security officers usually accompanied claimant and XXXXX to meeting locations.
propositions.quote: these six security officers usually accompanied them to the various locations where the claimant and XXXXX met.

propositions.text: Claimant was asked to explain inconsistency about noticing strange people in his narrative.
propositions.quote: the claimant was asked to explain why, in paragraph 10 of his narrative,2 he stated that he had [translation] "started noticing strange people" where he lived.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified about strange people outside his home identified as security staff, but was asked to explain inconsistency in his narrative.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant's narrative clearly alleged strangers outside his house, not that it was strange they were in his neighbourhood.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant clearly alleged in his narrative that the people outside his house were strange people or strangers, not [translation] "that it was strange that these people were in his neighbourhood."

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant's explanation for inconsistency unsatisfactory and flagrant.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant tried to brush aside the inconsistency, which the panel found to be flagrant.

propositions.text: It is reasonable to expect claimant to clearly disclose recognition of security officers if true.
propositions.quote: It is reasonable to expect the claimant to specifically and clearly disclose that he had recognized XXXXX security officers in his neighbourhood, if that was the case.

propositions.text: Panel concludes inconsistency undermines claimant's credibility.
propositions.quote: The panel concludes that the inconsistency between his testimony and the information in his narrative undermines his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's explanation for inconsistency flagrant and concludes it undermines his credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant initially testified telephone contact with XXXXX in 2008, then amended to no contact between those dates.
propositions.quote: the claimant initially testified that they had talked on the telephone on XXXX; he then amended his testimony and stated that there had not been any contact between these dates.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant initially said he talked on the phone with XXXXX in 2008, then changed to no contact between those dates.

propositions.text: Claimant said he threatened to reveal cards, gifts, photos from XXXXX after XXXXX was killed.
propositions.quote: He answered, [translation] "After XXXXX was killed."

propositions.text: Claimant was asked why narrative said threat was before XXXXX murder.
propositions.quote: the claimant was asked to explain why, in paragraph 11 of his narrative, he stated he had threatened XXXXX before XXXXX murder.

propositions.text: Claimant said he was stressed, confused events, threatened XXXXX on XXXX.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that he was stressed and nervous, that he had confused the events and that he had threatened XXXXX on XXXX.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant's explanation unsatisfactory for reasons given.
propositions.quote: This explanation does not satisfy the panel, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said he threatened XXXXX after murder but narrative said before; panel finds his explanation unsatisfactory.

propositions.text: Claimant should speak about alleged experiences with consistency, integrity and accuracy.
propositions.quote: It is reasonable to expect the claimant to speak about his alleged experiences with consistency, integrity and accuracy, since, according to his testimony, these events are the reason he does not want to return to his country.

paragraphs.summary: The panel states claimant should be consistent, accurate and truthful about his alleged experiences.

propositions.text: Claimant sought refuge with friend on XXXXX; warned by XXXXX to return; fled to friend's home in XXXXX.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that he sought refuge with a friend on XXXXX. He added that on XXXXX, XXXXX called him on his cellphone to warn him to return and that this was when he decided to flee from XXXXX and go to a friend's home in XXXXX.

propositions.text: Claimant stayed in XXXXX for 2-3 days; XXXXX called and warned he knew claimant's location and ordered return.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he stayed in XXXXX for two or three days, and that on XXXXX, 2008, XXXXX called and warned him that he knew where he was and ordered him to return to XXXXX.

propositions.text: Claimant changed phone number but XXXXX called him in XXXXX, demanding photos and gifts within 24 hours or death threat.
propositions.quote: And although the claimant changed his telephone number, XXXXX managed to call him on XXXXX, while he was still in XXXXXXX, because he wanted the claimant to give him the photographs and gifts that he had given him within 24 hours or else he would kill him.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified he fled to a friend's home after warnings and death threats from XXXXX demanding photos and gifts.

propositions.text: Claimant told XXXXX he had photos but had deleted them from camera.
propositions.quote: The claimant subsequently testified that he had told XXXXX that he had the photographs; however, he had already deleted the photographs from his camera.

propositions.text: Claimant was asked why no mention of photos in paragraph 15 of narrative.
propositions.quote: When asked why there is no mention of any photographs in paragraph 15 of his narrative, the claimant answered, [translation] "I do not know."

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant's explanation unsatisfactory for reasons given.
propositions.quote: This explanation does not satisfy the panel, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said he deleted photos but gave no explanation for their absence in narrative; panel finds explanation unsatisfactory.

propositions.text: Claimant alleged XXXXX wanted to resume romantic relationship and killed XXXXX for that reason alone.
propositions.quote: Throughout both his narrative and his testimony, the claimant alleged that XXXXX adamantly wanted to resume his romantic relationship with him. In the claimant's written allegations, XXXXX killed XXXXX for this reason alone.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleged XXXXX wanted to resume relationship and killed XXXXX for that reason alone.

propositions.text: In narrative, claimant said XXXXX threatened to kill him in 24 hours.
propositions.quote: in paragraph 15 of his narrative, the claimant stated that XXXXX last threats were "he told me he was going to kill me in 24 hours".

propositions.text: Claimant later said XXXXX wanted incriminating photos, adding new element to story.
propositions.quote: the claimant suddenly stated that what XXXXXX wanted was the incriminating [translation] "photographs."

propositions.text: Panel concludes claimant added new element to embellish claim and is not credible.
propositions.quote: The panel concludes that the claimant added a new element to his story to embellish his refugee protection claim. The claimant is not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant added new element about photos to embellish claim and is not credible.

propositions.text: Claimant said XXXXX was killed by gunshot and newspaper reported it as attempted theft.
propositions.quote: When asked how XXXXX was killed, the claimant answered, [translation] "by gunshot." When asked whether the murder had been reported in the Mexican newspapers, the claimant testified that one newspaper report had described his murder as an attempted theft.

propositions.text: Claimant did not submit newspaper article because XXXXX name was not mentioned and he did not keep it.
propositions.quote: he had not kept the article in question.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant said XXXXX was shot and newspaper reported attempted theft; he did not submit article as name was not mentioned.

propositions.text: Claimant submitted faxed email from "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" dated 2011 to corroborate XXXXX murder.
propositions.quote: the claimant submitted a faxed copy of an email from "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX," dated XXXXX, 2011.

propositions.text: Panel attaches little probative value to this document for reasons given.
propositions.quote: The panel attaches little probative value to this document, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant submitted a faxed email to corroborate murder; panel gives it little probative value.

propositions.text: Rule 28(1) requires documents in English or French or with translation and translator's declaration.
propositions.quote: subrule 28(1) of the Refugee Protection Division Rules states the following: All documents used at a proceeding must be in English or French or, if in another language, be provided with an English or French translation and a translator's declaration.

paragraphs.summary: Rule 28(1) requires documents be in English/French or have translation and translator's declaration.

propositions.text: No translator's declaration was provided as required by rule 28.
propositions.quote: No translator's declaration was provided in accordance with the requirements of rule 28.

paragraphs.summary: No translator's declaration was provided as required by rule 28.

propositions.text: Claimant testified person named XXXXXX was a lawyer, friend of a friend.
propositions.quote: the claimant testified that he was a lawyer, [translation] "a friend of a friend."

propositions.text: Document lacks header, address, or signature page typical of law firms, reducing probative value.
propositions.quote: The document does not contain a header, an address or even a personalized signature page, which is a relatively common practice for law firms and which would have indicated to the panel that this was indeed a legal, probative and relevant document.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant said author was a lawyer friend; document lacks typical law firm features, reducing probative value.

propositions.text: Document mentions deceased boyfriend and estate but lacks evidence establishing murder as described.
propositions.quote: the panel is of the opinion that there is no evidence in this document establishing that XXXXX was murdered as the claimant described.

paragraphs.summary: Document mentions deceased boyfriend and estate but lacks evidence establishing murder as described.

propositions.text: Claimant submitted another faxed email from a friend in Mexico dated 2011.
propositions.quote: the claimant also submitted into evidence, at the outset of the hearing, another fax of a copy of an email from "XXXXXXXXXXXXXX," dated XXXXXX, 2011.

propositions.text: Panel attaches little probative value to this document for reasons given.
propositions.quote: The panel attaches little probative value to this document, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant submitted another faxed email from a friend; panel gives it little probative value.

propositions.text: No translator's declaration provided as required by rule 28.
propositions.quote: Once again, no translator's declaration was provided in accordance with the requirements of rule 28.

propositions.text: Content is subjective, not from independent reliable source, produced to embellish claim.
propositions.quote: the content of this document, produced only one week before the hearing, is highly subjective and does not come from an independent and reliable source. Based on the inconsistencies in this file, the panel concludes that this document was produced solely for the purpose of embellishing the refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: No translator's declaration; document subjective, unreliable, produced to embellish claim, panel finds.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he had not travelled outside Mexico before Canada in 2008.
propositions.quote: he testified that he had not.

propositions.text: Panel asked why passport was issued five weeks before leaving for Canada.
propositions.quote: he was asked why his passport was issued to him on XXXXXX, 2008, five weeks before he left for Canada.

propositions.text: Claimant said he planned to travel with XXXXX to Cuba for vacation in July 2008.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that he had planned to travel with XXXXX to Cuba for a vacation at the end of July 2008.

propositions.text: Panel concludes claimant intended to travel to Canada, not Cuba, and invented persecution story to submit refugee claim.
propositions.quote: the panel concludes that the claimant was intending to travel to Canada on XXXXXX, 2008, and not to Cuba, as alleged; he invented his story of being persecuted by XXXXX for the purpose of submitting a refugee protection claim one month after he arrived in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant intended to travel to Canada, not Cuba, and invented persecution story to submit refugee claim.

propositions.text: State is presumed capable of protecting citizens except in complete state breakdown situations.
propositions.quote: It should be assumed that the state is capable of protecting its citizens, except in situations of complete breakdown of the state apparatus.

propositions.text: International protection applies only if claimant has no alternative protection.
propositions.quote: The presumption that a state is capable of protecting its citizens reinforces the principle that international protection comes into play only if the claimant has no alternative.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the presumption that states can protect citizens except in total breakdown, so international protection applies only if no alternative exists.

propositions.text: A claimant alleging inadequate state protection must prove it on a balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: A claimant who alleges that state protection is inadequate must satisfy the Board that, on a balance of probabilities, the evidence establishes that state protection is inadequate.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker states that a claimant must prove state protection is inadequate on a balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: The claimant testified he did not file a complaint due to XXXXX's influence in Mexico.
propositions.quote: the claimant testified that he had not filed a complaint with the Mexican authorities because it was not worth it, given XXXXX influence in Mexico.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimant's assertion of XXXXX's influence insufficient to justify not seeking protection.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant's assertion that XXXXX had too much influence in Mexico is insufficient not to try to make use of all possible courses of action to obtain protection

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker notes the claimant's testimony about XXXXX's influence but finds it insufficient to justify not seeking protection.

propositions.text: Even if XXXXX is influential, his influence is limited to one state; claimant could seek protection elsewhere in Mexico.
propositions.quote: Even if the panel believed that XXXXX was an influential politician, the fact remains that his influence would have been limited to the state of XXXXXXXX

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds XXXXX's influence limited and claimant could seek protection in another Mexican state.

propositions.text: The panel rejects the claimant's explanation as insufficient to explain why he did not seek protection before leaving Mexico.
propositions.quote: The panel rejects the claimant's explanation, finding it insufficient to explain why the claimant concluded that the authorities would not act on his complaint before he left his country.

propositions.text: The claimant failed to exhaust all possible courses of action before seeking international protection.
propositions.quote: the claimant failed to exhaust all possible courses of action in his country before seeking international protection.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker rejects the claimant's explanation and finds he failed to exhaust all protection options before leaving Mexico.

propositions.text: Claimant must show he took all reasonable steps to seek state protection and demonstrate interaction with authorities.
propositions.quote: The claimant must demonstrate that he has taken all reasonable steps in the circumstances to seek state protection, given the context of the country in general.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker states the claimant must show he took all reasonable steps to seek state protection and interaction with authorities.

propositions.text: Mexico functions normally and is presumed capable of protecting citizens.
propositions.quote: Mexico, a country that, according to the documentation, functions normally and is not in a situation of complete breakdown.

propositions.text: Claimant must seek state protection before claiming refugee protection elsewhere when country functions normally.
propositions.quote: Therefore, the claimant's country is presumed to be capable of protecting him, and this requires him to seek this protection before claiming refugee protection elsewhere

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows Mexico is making efforts to protect citizens and enable complaints.
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence shows that Mexico is making an effort to protect its citizens, by putting structures in place and adopting measures to enable citizens to file complaints.

propositions.text: No evidence shows claimant made serious effort or exhausted all courses to obtain state protection.
propositions.quote: there is nothing in the written or oral evidence demonstrating that the claimant made a serious and sufficient effort to obtain state protection or that he exhausted all courses of action open to him.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds Mexico functions normally, claimant must seek protection first, but claimant made no serious effort to do so.

propositions.text: Claimant did not make sufficient effort or exhaust all courses to obtain state protection.
propositions.quote: the claimant did not make a serious and sufficient effort to obtain state protection and that the claimant did not exhaust all courses of action open to him in his country

propositions.text: Claimant failed to rebut presumption that Mexico can protect him.
propositions.quote: the panel finds that the claimant was unable to discharge his burden of rebutting the presumption of protection that the state of Mexico would be able to offer him.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant failed to make sufficient effort and failed to rebut presumption Mexico can protect him.

propositions.text: To rebut presumption, claimant must provide clear and convincing evidence of state's inability to protect.
propositions.quote: To rebut the presumption of state protection, the claimant must provide "clear and convincing" evidence of the state's inability to protect

propositions.text: Evidence must be reliable, probative, and satisfy balance of probabilities standard.
propositions.quote: The evidence that state protection is inadequate must not only be reliable and have probative value, but must also satisfy the Board that, on a balance of probabilities, state protection is inadequate.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker states claimant must provide clear, convincing, reliable evidence to rebut presumption of state protection inadequacy.

propositions.text: Claimant did not provide clear and convincing evidence that Mexico cannot or will not protect him.
propositions.quote: the panel concludes that the claimant did not provide "clear and convincing" evidence that the Mexican state cannot or will not protect him.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker concludes claimant did not provide clear and convincing evidence that Mexico cannot protect him.

propositions.text: Claimant stated he faced discrimination due to sexual orientation including mistreatment and family rejection.
propositions.quote: the claimant stated that, because of his sexual orientation, he faced discrimination in his environment for years... his parents beat him and threw him out of the house

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker recounts claimant's allegations of discrimination and family rejection due to his sexual orientation.

propositions.text: Panel accepts claimant is homosexual but finds discrimination allegations exaggerated to embellish claim.
propositions.quote: the panel accepts that the claimant is homosexual, it finds that the allegations of discrimination against him were exaggerated to embellish his claim

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker accepts claimant's homosexuality but finds discrimination claims exaggerated.

propositions.text: Claimant amended PIF to show multiple schools and jobs but earlier stated only three schools attended.
propositions.quote: the claimant submitted amendments to his Personal Information Form (PIF) to point out that he had attended six schools... but at question 6 of his PIF, the claimant mentioned that he has 12 years of education, after attending one elementary school, one secondary school and one college.

propositions.text: Panel sees nothing extraordinary about claimant's school career.
propositions.quote: The panel sees nothing extraordinary about his school career.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker notes claimant's inconsistent school and work history and finds nothing extraordinary about his schooling.

propositions.text: Claimant provided same info in Schedule 1 as initial PIF, despite amendments.
propositions.quote: The information provided by the claimant at page 5 of the document Schedule 1... is the same information that he provided in his initial PIF.

propositions.text: Claimant said he did not pay attention to discrepancies when asked.
propositions.quote: the claimant answered that he had not paid attention.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant's explanation unsatisfactory for last-minute amendments.
propositions.quote: This explanation does not satisfy the panel, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant's explanation for inconsistent information unsatisfactory.

propositions.text: Claimant declared information was complete and true when submitted.
propositions.quote: When the claimant provided the information requested in this form, he declared that the information he gave was complete, true and correct.

propositions.text: Panel finds it unreasonable claimant waited until hearing day to amend basic info.
propositions.quote: it is unreasonable for the claimant to wait until the day before his hearing to amend information as basic as his education and his list of employers.

propositions.text: Panel concludes amendments were last-minute to harmonize allegations about homosexuality.
propositions.quote: The panel concludes that the amendments were made at the last minute to harmonize the allegations in his narrative with respect to his homosexuality.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant's last-minute amendments unreasonable and likely to embellish his claim.

propositions.text: Claimant answered 'XXXXXXXXX' when asked who he feared if returned to country, no mention of discrimination.
propositions.quote: when asked, "Who are you afraid of if you were to return to your country?" the claimant answered "XXXXXXXXX" There is no mention of discrimination or of persecution based on his homosexuality.

propositions.text: Claimant gave no satisfactory reason for not mentioning sexual orientation fear.
propositions.quote: The claimant did not have a satisfactory reason when he was asked to explain why he did not mention his sexual orientation.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant did not mention fear based on sexual orientation and gave no satisfactory explanation.

propositions.text: Panel concludes alleged discrimination does not amount to persecution.
propositions.quote: the panel concludes that the discrimination alleged by the claimant does not amount to persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker concludes claimant's alleged discrimination does not amount to persecution.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant has an internal flight alternative in Mexico.
propositions.quote: the panel is of the opinion that the claimant has an internal flight alternative in Mexico.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker finds claimant has an internal flight alternative in Mexico.

propositions.text: Claimant was asked about fears if living elsewhere in Mexico, such as La Paz or Mexico City.
propositions.quote: the claimant was asked what he might fear if he returned and lived elsewhere in Mexico, such as in the city of La Paz... or in Mexico City

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker notes claimant was asked about fears living elsewhere in Mexico.

propositions.text: Claimant testified XXXXX could find him anywhere in Mexico.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that XXXXX would be able to find him anywhere in Mexico.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker notes claimant testified XXXXX could find him anywhere in Mexico.

propositions.text: Claimant gave no reason why it would be unreasonable to seek refuge in other cities within the meaning of case law.
propositions.quote: the claimant submitted no reason why it would be unreasonable, within the meaning of the case law,11 to go to one of these cities to seek refuge

propositions.text: Claimant submitted no real and concrete evidence of risk of persecution or risk to life or cruel treatment.
propositions.quote: He also submitted no real and concrete evidence establishing the existence of conditions making it possible that he could run the risk of being persecuted on a Convention ground or face a risk to his life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant gave no reason or evidence showing it would be unreasonable to seek refuge elsewhere or that he faces persecution risk.

propositions.text: Burden of proof on internal flight alternative rests on claimant to show unreasonableness or conditions preventing relocation.
propositions.quote: The burden of proof regarding an internal flight alternative rests on the claimant. Thus, the applicant had to establish either that it would be unreasonable for him to seek refuge in another part of the country or that there were, in fact, conditions preventing him from relocating elsewhere.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Justice Lagacé in Ramirez that claimant bears burden to prove internal flight alternative is unreasonable or impossible.

propositions.text: It is settled law that burden of proof on internal flight alternative is on applicant to show unreasonableness of seeking refuge elsewhere.
propositions.quote: It is settled law that in matters concerning internal flight alternatives the burden of proof is on the applicant.... Therefore, the refugee claimant must demonstrate that it would be unreasonable for him or her to seek refuge in a different part of the country.

paragraphs.summary: Justice Shore in Palacios confirms burden is on claimant to prove unreasonableness of internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: Claimant must show on balance of probabilities a serious risk of persecution in part of country with internal flight alternative.
propositions.quote: the Court of Appeal established that the onus is on the claimant to demonstrate why, on a balance of probabilities, he faces a serious risk of persecution in a part of the country where there might be an internal flight alternative.

paragraphs.summary: Court of Appeal in Thirunavukkarasu holds claimant must prove serious risk of persecution where internal flight alternative exists.

propositions.text: Claimant is 26 years old with 12 years education and 5 years labour experience in Mexico.
propositions.quote: The claimant is a 26-year-old man with 12 years of education and 5 years of labour market experience in Mexico

paragraphs.summary: The court states claimant's age, education, and labour market experience in Mexico.

propositions.text: Panel does not believe incidents occurred in 2008 or that claimant still has interest from XXXXX given time passed.
propositions.quote: the panel does not believe that XXXXX still has any interest in the claimant, given the passage of time.

paragraphs.summary: The panel disbelieves the incidents occurred and that XXXXX still has interest in claimant due to time elapsed.

propositions.text: Claimant did not discharge burden of proof and has an internal flight alternative.
propositions.quote: the claimant did not discharge his burden of proof, as set out in the case law,15 and concludes that he has an internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: Internal flight alternative alone is sufficient to dispose of refugee claim under section 96 or subsection 97(1) IRPA.
propositions.quote: This is a fatal consideration that "...is in itself sufficient to dispose of the refugee claim," as stated by the Honourable Justice Shore in Palacios,16 above, under either section 96 or subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant failed burden and has internal flight alternative, which alone suffices to reject claim under IRPA.

propositions.text: Claimant cannot succeed; fear has no objective basis as he can avail state protection.
propositions.quote: I determine that the claimant, XXXXXXXXXXXXXX, cannot succeed. The claimant's fear has no objective basis, whether under section 96 or section 97 of the IRPA, because he can avail himself of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant cannot succeed as his fear lacks objective basis and state protection is available.

propositions.text: Refugee protection claim is rejected.
propositions.quote: Consequently, his refugee protection claim is rejected.

paragraphs.summary: The court orders rejection of the refugee protection claim.
